newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Herzog says sure Hungary to be among first to join EU.
newsitem.headline: Herzog says sure Hungary to be among first to join EU.

text.p: German president Roman Herzog told Hungary on Tuesday he was sure it would be one of the first new members of the European Union.

"Hungary will enjoy the support of Germany for its integration into European Union and NATO," Herzog said in a speech to Hungary's parliament. "I am sure Hungary will be one of the first candidates to be admitted to the EU and NATO."
Herzog said he was impressed by the perseverance Hungary had shown in its efforts towards European integration and described its legislation on minority rights as exemplary.
"An unmistakeable sign of the maturity of the new Hungarian democracy is the way Hungary treats its minorities," he said. "The legislation can serve as a model for the whole of eastern Europe."

Hungary was one of the first post-communist states of central and eastern Europe to adopt Council of Europe legisalative norms for the protection of language education and cultural and political rights for ethnic minorities in the country.
Herzog arrived in Hungary on Tuesday to begin a three-day official visit during which the subject of minority rights will play an important role.

Later on Tuesday he will visit the Budapest synagogue, the largest in Europe and on Wednesday he will visit the German speaking Schwab community in the village of Solymar, near Budapest, and hold talks with leaders of Hungary's other ethnic minorities.
Herzog said earlier Budapest's improved relations with its neighbours had dispelled fears that the European Union would import regional tensions if it expanded eastwards.

"Three or four years ago when the European Union first discussed allowing new members from Central and Eastern Europe there were fears that these new incoming countries would bring in tensions," he told reporters after meeting Hungarian president Arpad Goncz.
"Hungary's minorities policy has created a situation whereby these fears...have now disappeared."
Herzog made a specific appeal in his speech to Parliament that Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary to be allowed to become an integral part of Europe.
"Europe cannot be complete unless Budapest, Prague and Warsaw belong to it as well -- this is not a romantic dream but the imperative of reality," he said.

Herzog added that in a unified Europe, Russia and the Ukraine also had to find "a firm place" and encouraged current efforts by NATO to build a security partnership which defines the areas of cooperation and sets mechanisms for consultation.
